note: Attacker-controlled 4 bytes from the PoC set parser options; XML_PARSE_DTDVALID is ORed in, enabling DTD validation.
The first URL/entity pair from the PoC supplies the XML document containing a DTD and an element attribute with a non-ASCII value.

code: doc = xmlCtxtReadMemory(ctxt, docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts & ~XML_PARSE_DTDVALID);
note: Document is parsed without DTDVALID so validation is deferred to the explicit post-validation pass.
Post-validation triggers xmlValidateDocument which walks the tree and validates each element.
For each attribute with children, the attribute value is serialized with inLine=0, which sets escape=1 and, since doc->encoding is NULL, adds XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII.
The attribute's text node content (containing a non-ASCII byte >= 0x80) is passed to xmlEscapeText with XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII set.
Inside the while loop, a stack-allocated 12-byte buffer is declared in the else branch for serializing a hex char reference of the non-ASCII character.
repl is set to point at the stack buffer tempBuf; tempBuf's scope ends when the else block closes.
After the else block, memcpy reads replSize bytes from repl, which points to the out-of-scope stack buffer tempBuf, causing a stack-use-after-scope read.
